In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Non-programmable calculators are allowed. Duration: two and a half hours.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Given the functions $f$ and $g$, defined as $f(x)=x-3,\ x\in\mathbb{R}$ and $g(x)=2x+1,\ x\in\mathbb{R}$,

find,

(a) $f(4)$

questions.corrige_markdown:
$fg(x)=f(g(x))$: apply $g$ first, then $f$.

$fg(x)=f(2x+1)=(2x+1)-3=2x-2$.

**Answer: $fg(x)=2x-2$.** (Do not confuse it with $gf(x)=2(x-3)+1=2x-5$.)

Let $y=g(x)=2x+1$. Make $x$ the subject: $y-1=2x$, so $x=\dfrac{y-1}{2}$.

Replace $y$ by $x$: $g^{-1}(x)=\dfrac{x-1}{2}$.

Check: $g\left(\dfrac{x-1}{2}\right)=2\cdot\dfrac{x-1}{2}+1=x$.

**Answer: $g^{-1}(x)=\dfrac{x-1}{2}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) Figure 1 is a Venn diagram representing the number of students in a certain class of 30.

$P=\{\text{Students studying Physics}\}$

$C=\{\text{Students studying Chemistry}\}$

(a) Write, in set notation, the total number of students in the class.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The universal set $\xi$ is the whole class, which has 30 students.

**Answer: $n(\xi)=30$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) Write down an equation in terms of $x$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Add all the regions of the diagram: only $P$: $x$; both: $4$; only $C$: $5$; neither: $2x$.

$x+4+5+2x=30$, that is $3x+9=30$.

**Answer: $3x+9=30$** (equivalently $x+4+5+2x=30$).

questions.enonce_markdown: (d) Find, how many students study neither Physics nor Chemistry.
(e) Determine the number of students studying one subject only. *[9 marks for (ii)]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Only Physics $=x=7$ and only Chemistry $=5$, so one subject only $=7+5=12$.

Check: $7+4+5+14=30$.

**Answer: 12 students.**
